sources.institution: All state agencies on state payroll, including VCCS colleges and universities (shown by agency)
sources.system: Commonwealth Data Point (Auditor of Public Accounts)
sources.download_url: No bulk file. The page queries salaryConnection.php by POST (AngularJS app).
sources.coverage_years: FY2017 to about FY2022 in the new portal (the VT library FAQ says Virginia Tech's latest year is 2022); earlier years in the legacy portal
sources.blocker: No employee names (anonymized IDs only), and access is through an interactive query form with no bulk export.
sources.notes: Official, but not person-level by name. Useful only for position-level aggregates.

sources.institution: UVA (incl. medical center, UVA-Wise), GMU, JMU, ODU, VCU, Radford, Virginia Tech and others, plus all DOA-payroll agencies including VCCS
sources.system: Virginia Center for Investigative Journalism at WHRO (news database)
sources.institutions_covered: about 170,000 state employees including public universities
sources.employees: all (caveats: Radford and JMU base salary only; VCU excludes people earning $10,000 or less)
sources.blocker: Search-only news tool. The article URL returned 404 on 2026-10-17 (it may have moved), and no download link was found.
sources.notes: Built from Department of Accounts payroll plus public-records requests to each independent university payroll. VCIJ might share the dataset on request.

sources.blocker: Third-party paginated HTML; coverage of Virginia universities not verified.

gaps: No official named, person-level pay file for any Virginia public university or VCCS. Data Point drops names. The only named data is the VCIJ/WHRO 2025 search tool (and older Richmond Times-Dispatch and Washington Business Journal databases), all search-only. Would need Virginia FOIA requests to each university, which run their own payroll.
notes: Checked data.virginia.gov (CKAN): only city salary datasets (Norfolk, Virginia Beach). Data Point salaries rated C because it has no names. The VCIJ article is the best named source but has no download. University library FAQs (e.g., Virginia Tech) point to Data Point and say it lacks names and departments.
